newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan market higher on improved demand.
newsitem.headline: Jordan market higher on improved demand.

text.p: Jordanian shares were firmer on Monday buoyed by mostly local investor demand focused on solid firms with high earnings forecasts, brokers said.

The official Amman Financial Market (AFM) index rose 0.28 percent to 152.57 points in moderate turnover of 427,465 dinars ($603,764) dominated by healthy demand on select blue chip and companies expected to perform well in 1997.

The exchange also continued a pattern of bargain hunting activity by mostly local investors in a handful of speculative and blue-chip stock prompted by recent falls which have made current price levels attractive, brokers said.
Political uncertainty combined with a lack of liquidity has recently depressed sentiment and prompted outside buyers and institutional investors to remain on the sidelines.
The busiest stock was Jordan Ceramic Factories which rose 0.10 dinars to 7.05 dinars in a bloc sale worth 53,732 dinars.

Another high performer was blue-chip Jordan Cement Factories which rose 0.08 dinars to 3.59 dinars on reports the government was readjusting higher fixed prices of cement which is expected to boost the firm's profitability.
Other stocks which witnessed active deals in an otherwise quiet trading day were Shipping Line which was unchanged at 2.35 dinars in trade worth 36,777 dinars.
Jordan Electric Power rose 0.01 dinars to 1.68 in trade worth 27,085 dinars.

In banks, Housing Bank led the sector rising 0.04 dinars to 4.90 dinars, continuing a pattern of demand on expectation its transformation into a comprehensive bank will expand its commercial banking business base.
Market heavyweight Arab Bank dropped a marginal 0.25 dinars to 255.75 dinars in trade worth 30,665 dinars.
The market on Monday saw 14 shares rising against an equal number falling. Another 16 were traded but closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance rose 0.38 percent to 80.46 points, 3.52 percent down from the start of the year.
